introduction: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sorts people by what they have heard, and Bahá’u’lláh asks why those who heard so often refused: they followed their leaders, they did not examine the matter in their own hearts, they could not see past the garb of an ordinary man. From there the readings go to the leaders themselves, to accusation and evidence, to beatings, stonings and exile, to the prudence of hiding and emigrating, to a people who let themselves be killed rather than kill, and to prayers of lament. The pattern is old. Stephen asks which of the prophets was not persecuted; the Qur’an says that no messenger came but was mocked; Socrates, Amos, Elijah, Paul and the Christians under Nero are here, with Tertullian on scapegoats and blood as seed. So are those who answered persecution with principle: Locke, Jefferson, Washington, the Universal Declaration, and Nicodemus asking whether the law judges a man unheard. The readings are questioned too. Mill calls it a pleasant falsehood that truth always survives persecution; Daniel prays at an open window where the readings counsel hiding; the Qur’an permits the wronged to fight; Burke defends trust in one’s teachers; and Paul will not let the guilt of some become the rejection of a people.
questions: Bahá’u’lláh says that people would have found guidance had they not followed their divines. Burke defends relying on inherited judgment, and Paul bound his churches to reject new gospels. How, on the readings’ account, should a faithful person examine a new claim?
The same passage that calls false leaders wolves honours true ones as “eyes to the nations”. With Malachi, Chaucer’s parson and Shakespeare’s “brief authority” in mind, what marks the difference?

‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes that interference in matters of conscience strengthens what it attacks; Tertullian agrees; Mill calls this a pleasant falsehood. What is the evidence on each side, and what should no one conclude from the first view?
The Báb tells his followers to emigrate or hide; the friends meet in hidden places; Daniel opens his window. What considerations decide between prudence and open witness?

“The people of God suffered themselves to be killed rather than kill.” The Qur’an allows the wronged to fight so that houses of worship are not pulled down. Is there one answer for the victim and another for the bystander with power?
A governor protests an unjust sentence; Nicodemus asks for a hearing; Pilate washes his hands. What do the readings and these figures ask of people who are neither persecutor nor persecuted?

outside.why: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishes those who heard and did not accept from those who have not yet heard. Jesus’ parable sorts hearers the same way, by the ground the seed fell on.
The divines objected that the signs handed down in their traditions “had not appeared”. John records the same argument made from scripture: shall Christ come out of Galilee?
“Had they refused to follow in the footsteps of the abject and foolish among their leaders and divines.” Jesus: they be blind leaders of the blind.
They “neglected to examine the matter in their own hearts”. Kant called that neglect a self-incurred tutelage, and its cure courage: dare to use your own reason.

The reading blames people for following their leaders and not their own examination. Burke thought the private stock of reason in each person small, and that people do well to draw on the bank of ages. When is trusting one’s teachers wise, and when is it the failure the reading describes?
“At no time, in no Dispensation, have the Prophets of God escaped … the denunciation of the learned of their age.” Stephen to the council: which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted?
The Qur’an states the rule as a lament: never came there unto them a messenger but they did mock him.
The persecutors “appeared in the guise of uprightness and piety”. Jesus describes that piety: building the tombs of the prophets, and saying, we would not have been partakers in their blood.
The Báb’s sentence is taken from this verse of the Qur’an: none entereth paradise unless he be a Jew or a Christian. These are their own desires.
“How many houses were raised for My remembrance … yet when I revealed Myself they barred Me from them.” The Apocalypse, to a church: behold, I stand at the door, and knock.
They spent beyond reckoning to exalt His remembrance and refused Him when He came. Dostoevsky’s Grand Inquisitor tells the returned Christ the same to his face: why art Thou come to hinder us?
“They have regarded the essence of justice as the substance of tyranny, and light they have deemed darkness.” Isaiah: woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light.
Even if people acknowledged the truth, “it would be merely through imitation”. Mill says the same of any true opinion held without examination: a dead dogma, not a living truth.

“This Most Great Revelation hath ever been … independent of the acceptance or rejection of the peoples.” Gamaliel’s advice to the council rests on that independence: if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.

They were “deluded by the appearance of the peerless and everlasting Beauty in the garb of mortal men”. Nazareth on its neighbour: is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? And they were offended at him.

The reading blames those who fail to recognize a new Manifestation. Paul had bound his churches to reject any new gospel, though an angel brought it. A believer who refuses a later claim may be obeying that charge. How do the readings ask such a person to proceed?
“Beware lest ye shut out the people by yet another veil.” Jesus to the scribes: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men; ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering.
“Instead of evincing self-denial they have given themselves up to inordinate desires.” Ezekiel: woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?
“He hath repudiated the divines.” The priest of Bethel reports Amos to the king in the same tone: the land is not able to bear all his words.
“Wherefore do ye wear the guise of the shepherd, when inwardly ye have become wolves?” Jesus: ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward.
False shepherds are a star that “leadeth the wayfarers of My city astray”. Milton on the clergy of his day: blind mouths! The hungry sheep look up, and are not fed.
Micah’s charge is specific: the priests teach for hire, and the prophets divine for money, yet will they lean upon the Lord.
Isabella on anyone given office over others: man, proud man, drest in a little brief authority, most ignorant of what he’s most assured.

The same passage honours divines “truly adorned with the ornament of knowledge and of a goodly character”, who are “as eyes to the nations”. Malachi states what the office is for before he says how it failed: the priest’s lips should keep knowledge. How does one tell the two kinds apart?
Chaucer, no friend of the clergy he knew, drew one such: the poor parson who first wrought and afterward taught. What does the reading’s praise of true divines guard against in its own denunciations?

Bahá’u’lláh says that His opponents have done “what even the people of the Qur’án dared not do to Myself, nor the Jews to Christ”. Paul, speaking of his own people after the crucifixion, refuses to let the charge become a verdict on a people: hath God cast away his people? God forbid.
This is the first taunt ‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes from the Qur’an: ye follow but a man bewitched.
And this the last: is this he whom Allah sendeth as a messenger?
Opponents “would impute folly and impotence to the divine Manifestations”. The Pharisees of a healing they could not deny: this fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub.
A governor had “a document containing strange allegations” sent secretly to court. Daniel’s rivals, finding no fault in him, look for an occasion “concerning the law of his God”.

“Cruel and incessant darts are being hurled against me from every point”, while his heart overflows with love for his friends. The psalm: for my love they are my adversaries: but I give myself unto prayer.

The Báb’s missionaries were beaten, their beards burnt, and “led … round the streets and bazaars”. Tacitus, no friend of the Christians, on what Nero did to them: mockery of every sort was added to their deaths.
Paul’s own list: thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils in the city.
The Epistle to the Hebrews on those so treated: they had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, of whom the world was not worthy.
Burns gave English its phrase for it: man’s inhumanity to man makes countless thousands mourn.

“Interference in matters of conscience causes stability and firmness and attracts the attention of men’s sight and souls.” Tertullian to the magistrates: the oftener we are mown down by you, the more in number we grow.
The doctors “thought that violence … would cause extinction and silence”. After Stephen’s death the church was scattered, and they that were scattered went every where preaching the word.

‘Abdu’l-Bahá holds that persecution strengthens what it attacks. Mill calls that a pleasant falsehood: history teems with instances of truth put down by persecution. Which movements does each remember, and what follows for those who are being persecuted now?
“The doctors of Persia have no administrative capacity”: they used force in a matter where force has no place. Locke: the care of souls does not belong to the magistrate.
Jefferson drew the line where the reading draws it, at “matters of conscience”: it does me no injury for my neighbour to say there are twenty gods, or no god.
The scripture the doctors professed has the principle in five words: there is no compulsion in religion.
A century after these events the nations wrote the freedom down, including what the Bábís had done: freedom to change his religion or belief.
The townspeople “besieged the governor’s residence, pelted Us with stones”. Stephen under the stones: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
“It is incumbent upon him either to emigrate by God’s leave, or to hide himself.” Jesus to the twelve: when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The Qur’an presses the same counsel on those who stayed and were crushed: was not Allah’s earth spacious that ye could have migrated therein?

The Báb counsels his followers not to stir strife, and to emigrate or hide if threatened. Daniel, when the decree was signed, prayed at his open window “as he did aforetime”. What decides between the hidden place and the open window?

His brother “seized the pen of calumny”, attributing to him what he had himself done. Iago, of all people, on what calumny takes: he that filches from me my good name robs me of that which not enriches him and makes me poor indeed.

“He intended to martyr this Wronged One. Through pure grace and bounty I departed from among those souls.” Paul’s first escape: the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.
An official admits: “I have been unable to obtain any evidence.” Pilate: I find no fault in this man.
Enemies “from all the kindreds and peoples of the world, are growing aggressive”. Jesus: if the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.
Books “filled … with countless calumnies” are distributed, and he stands firm. Jesus: blessed are ye, when men shall say all manner of evil against you falsely.
If a House of Worship would arouse hostility, “the meeting must … be held in some hidden place”. The first Easter evening: the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled, for fear.
Obadiah, steward of a persecuting king, hid a hundred prophets by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.
“What a clamour the hypocrites have raised throughout the land.” Thessalonica on two travelling preachers: these that have turned the world upside down are come hither also.
“The rights of the people have been entirely lost.” Isaiah: truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.

“The deed of one ignorant one has caused all corruption to be attributed to this Wronged One.” Tertullian on the habit of blaming a minority: if the Tiber rises, if the Nile does not, the cry is, Away with the Christians to the lion!
“We are oppressed among Our enemies—be ye as We are.” Socrates is asked whether he would rather suffer injustice than do it, and says he would rather suffer.
“Aid your Lord through wisdom and utterance, and follow not the ways of the oppressors who shed blood.” Jesus at his arrest: put up again thy sword into his place.
The oppressed are not to become like their oppressors. The Qur’an: let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly.
“Proclaim what hath been prescribed unto thee … though all the peoples arise and oppose thee.” Socrates to his jury: I honor and love you; but I shall obey God rather than you.

“Great is the multitude who will rise up to oppose you … yet shall your heavenly Father confer upon you such spiritual illumination.” The eighth beatitude: blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake.

“The people of God suffered themselves to be killed rather than kill” and “interceded on behalf of the murderers”. The First Letter of Peter: when he was reviled, he reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not.
“Absolute meekness yieldeth many a result.” The Dhammapada calls it an old rule: hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love.

Bahá’u’lláh praises a people who would not defend themselves by arms. The Qur’an gives the wronged leave to fight, and its reason: otherwise cloisters and churches and oratories and mosques would have been pulled down. When is the defence of the persecuted by force a duty, and whose?
“Give to the executioner thy head, but not thy heart.” Jesus: fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.

“He Who hath come to build anew the whole world” is forced “to dwell within the most desolate of cities”. Jesus: the foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
All mankind “deserveth to be tormented and to perish”, and a loving providence protects it. Lamentations: it is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed.
“All that befell those of a former age must likewise befall you.” The Second Letter to Timothy: all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.

Some imagine “that calamities can deter Bahá from fulfilling that which God … hath purposed”. The Qur’an: fain would they put out the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light.

“The most effective means whereby this light of truth is safeguarded … is the onslaught of the enemies.” Paul in chains: the things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel.
Lowell’s couplet is the best known English form of the thought: truth forever on the scaffold, wrong forever on the throne; yet that scaffold sways the future.

The lamp’s globe is the wind; the ship’s safety is the storm. Ivan Karamazov will not accept any harmony that has to be paid for with the suffering of the innocent. This section is titled for “the limits of easy explanations”. What would make the reading’s explanation an easy one, and what keeps it from being so?
A governor asks what justification there is for condemning “a guest … who has not been given the chance to defend himself”. Nicodemus to the council: doth our law judge any man, before it hear him?
“What evidence have they with which to support their contention?” Festus states the Roman rule: not to deliver any man to die, before he have the accusers face to face.
In the Qur’an it is a man of Pharaoh’s own household who speaks up: would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah?
One official protests while the crowd demands a death. Hillel: in a place where there are no men, strive to be a man.
The governor in the reading remonstrates loudly. Pilate also found no fault, and when he saw a tumult rising took water and washed his hands. What separates the two men, and which is the commoner?
“Justice is tormented by the scourge of injustice.” King from a jail cell: injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.
Proverbs lays the duty on whoever has a voice: open thy mouth for the dumb, in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.

When “a far-from-perfect priesthood acquire control of affairs”, no one is safe. Washington to a synagogue, on a government built otherwise: it gives to bigotry no sanction, to persecution no assistance.

Two governments “arose against His Cause, and the result is that both … have been disintegrated”. Asked whose sin caused a man’s blindness, Jesus refused the inference from misfortune to guilt. How should the fall of a persecutor be read, and who is entitled to read it?
“Indeed it is proven that He is a fomenter of discord!” Ahab to Elijah: art thou he that troubleth Israel?
“This servant stands alone and solitary, facing the onslaught of all.” Elijah at Horeb: I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life.
“The Lote-Tree … crieth out, by reason of the cruelty of the divines.” Jeremiah: oh that mine eyes were a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain.
“The Pen is unable to move … and it weepeth sore.” Jesus beheld the city, and wept over it.
“Every morning I arose from My bed, I discovered the hosts of countless afflictions massed behind My door.” Paul: troubled on every side, yet not distressed; persecuted, but not forsaken.
He “hath neither the pity of His foes nor the compassion of His friends”. The psalm: it was not an enemy that reproached me; it was thou, mine acquaintance.

“What injustice have they committed? Whom have they betrayed? … they would know not what to answer.” Jesus to the officer who struck him: if I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?
The Qur’an of an earlier people burnt for their faith: they had naught against them save that they believed in Allah.
The wrongs of the oppressors “have come in between”. The Qur’an: deem not that Allah is unaware of what the wicked do.
Servants “sincere towards all humanity, even their enemies” are in “the claws of the ravening wolves”. Jesus: behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves.
The prayer asks protection for them. Mordecai tells a queen that the prayer may be answered through her: who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
They were “banished … and made … captives”. The Epistle to the Hebrews: remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them.
Banished from their cities, like the exiles who sat down by the rivers of Babylon and wept.
“Such is my love for Thee that I can fear no one, though the powers of all the worlds be arrayed against me.” The psalm: the Lord is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?
Three men before a king and a furnace: our God is able to deliver us; but if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods.
“Some turned away from me, others disowned my claim, a few hesitated.” The Qur’an to its Prophet: messengers indeed have been denied before thee, and they were patient.
“I know not, O my God, for what reason they have risen up to oppress me.” Jesus quotes a psalm for it: they hated me without a cause.
The inmates of heaven lament with him. In the Apocalypse the slain themselves cry out: how long, O Lord, holy and true?
The Báb gave his life that Another might appear, and “as soon as He came down” hands were stretched out against Him. The parable of the vineyard: last of all he sent unto them his son.

matthew-persecuted-for-righteousness.text: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven

john-if-the-world-hate-you.text: If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you

john-hated-me-without-a-cause.text: But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause

acts-which-of-the-prophets.text: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye. Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers

acts-stephen-stoned.text: Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, And cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep

acts-why-persecutest-thou-me.text: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks

acts-turned-the-world-upside-down.text: These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also; Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus

kings-troubleth-israel.text: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father's house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim

kings-i-only-am-left.text: And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away

amos-prophesy-not-again.text: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words. For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land. Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Bethel: for it is the king's chapel, and it is the king's court

isaiah-call-evil-good.text: Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter

isaiah-truth-is-fallen.text: And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey

psalm-for-my-love-my-adversaries.text: For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me: they have spoken against me with a lying tongue. They compassed me about also with words of hatred; and fought against me without a cause. For my love they are my adversaries: but I give myself unto prayer

psalm-i-am-for-peace.text: My soul hath long dwelt with him that hateth peace. I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war

matthew-by-beelzebub.text: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw. And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David? But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils

john-hath-a-devil.text: There was a division therefore again among the Jews for these sayings. And many of them said, He hath a devil, and is mad; why hear ye him? Others said, These are not the words of him that hath a devil. Can a devil open the eyes of the blind

luke-all-men-speak-well.text: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake. Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets. But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation. Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep. Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets

timothy-shall-suffer-persecution.text: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution

peter-think-it-not-strange.text: Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ's sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy. If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified. But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men's matters. Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf

peter-reviled-not-again.text: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously

corinthians-being-reviled-we-bless.text: Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace; And labour, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it: Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day

revelation-faithful-unto-death.text: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life

hebrews-remember-them-in-bonds.text: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body

proverbs-deliver-them-drawn-unto-death.text: If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works

proverbs-open-thy-mouth.text: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy

esther-such-a-time-as-this.text: Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews. For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father's house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this

john-doth-our-law-judge.text: Nicodemus saith unto them, (he that came to Jesus by night, being one of them,) Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth

acts-accusers-face-to-face.text: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him

luke-no-fault-in-this-man.text: Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man. And they were the more fierce, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place

matthew-washed-his-hands.text: When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it

acts-scattered-abroad.text: And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles. And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him. As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison. Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word

philippians-furtherance-of-the-gospel.text: But I would ye should understand, brethren, that the things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel; So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other places; And many of the brethren in the Lord, waxing confident by my bonds, are much more bold to speak the word without fear

acts-in-a-basket.text: And after that many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him: But their laying await was known of Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him. Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket

matthew-flee-into-egypt.text: And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt

kings-hid-them-in-a-cave.text: And Ahab called Obadiah, which was the governor of his house. (Now Obadiah feared the Lord greatly: For it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, that Obadiah took an hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water

john-why-smitest-thou-me.text: The high priest then asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his doctrine. Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing. Why askest thou me? ask them which heard me, what I have said unto them: behold, they know what I said. And when he had thus spoken, one of the officers which stood by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so? Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me

samuel-david-spares-saul.text: Behold, this day thine eyes have seen how that the Lord had delivered thee to day into mine hand in the cave: and some bade me kill thee: but mine eye spared thee; and I said, I will not put forth mine hand against my lord; for he is the Lord's anointed. Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, know thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in mine hand, and I have not sinned against thee; yet thou huntest my soul to take it. The Lord judge between me and thee, and the Lord avenge me of thee: but mine hand shall not be upon thee

daniel-no-occasion-against.text: Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him. Then said these men, We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God

quran-denied-before-thee.text: Messengers indeed have been denied before thee, and they were patient under the denial and the persecution till Our succour reached them. There is none to alter the decisions of Allah. Already there hath reached thee (somewhat) of the tidings of the messengers (We sent before).

quran-never-came-a-messenger.text: Ah, the anguish for the bondmen! Never came there unto them a messenger but they did mock him!

quran-wizard-or-madman.text: Even so there came no messenger unto those before them but they said: A wizard or a madman!

quran-man-bewitched.text: We are Best Aware of what they wish to hear when they give ear to thee and when they take secret counsel, when the evil-doers say: Ye follow but a man bewitched.

quran-is-this-he.text: And when they see thee (O Muhammad) they treat thee only as a jest (saying): Is this he whom Allah sendeth as a messenger?

quran-jew-or-christian.text: And they say: None entereth paradise unless he be a Jew or a Christian. These are their own desires. Say: Bring your proof (of what ye state) if ye are truthful.

quran-naught-against-them.text: They had naught against them save that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Owner of Praise,

quran-cloisters-and-churches.text: Those who have been driven from their homes unjustly only because they said: Our Lord is Allah - For had it not been for Allah's repelling some men by means of others, cloisters and churches and oratories and mosques, wherein the name of Allah is oft mentioned, would assuredly have been pulled down. Verily Allah helpeth one who helpeth Him. Lo! Allah is Strong, Almighty -

quran-would-ye-kill-a-man.text: And a believing man of Pharaoh's family, who hid his faith, said: Would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah, and hath brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is lying, then his lie is upon him; and if he is truthful, then some of that wherewith he threateneth you will strike you. Lo! Allah guideth not one who is a prodigal, a liar.

quran-earth-spacious.text: Lo! as for those whom the angels take (in death) while they wrong themselves, (the angels) will ask: In what were ye engaged? They will say: We were oppressed in the land. (The angels) will say: Was not Allah's earth spacious that ye could have migrated therein? As for such, their habitation will be hell, an evil journey's end;

quran-let-not-hatred.text: O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity, and let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly. Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty. Observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do.

quran-put-out-the-light.text: Fain would they put out the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light however much the disbelievers are averse.

quran-not-unaware.text: Deem not that Allah is unaware of what the wicked do. He but giveth them a respite till a day when eyes will stare (in terror),

plato-obey-god-rather-than-you.text: Men of Athens, I honor and love you; but I shall obey God rather than you, and while I have life and strength I shall never cease from the practice and teaching of philosophy
plato-obey-god-rather-than-you.author: Plato

tertullian-christians-to-the-lion.text: If the Tiber rises as high as the city walls, if the Nile does not send its waters up over the fields, if the heavens give no rain, if there is an earthquake, if there is famine or pestilence, straightway the cry is, Away with the Christians to the lion!
tertullian-christians-to-the-lion.author: Tertullian

milton-truth-and-falsehood-grapple.text: And though all the windes of doctrin were let loose to play upon the earth, so Truth be in the field, we do injuriously, by licencing and prohibiting to misdoubt her strength. Let her and Falshood grapple; who ever knew Truth put to the wors, in a free and open encounter
milton-truth-and-falsehood-grapple.author: John Milton

jefferson-twenty-gods-or-no-god.text: The legitimate powers of government extend to such acts only as are injurious to others. But it does me no injury for my neighbor to say there are twenty Gods, or no God. It neither picks my pocket nor breaks my leg
jefferson-twenty-gods-or-no-god.author: Thomas Jefferson
jefferson-twenty-gods-or-no-god.work: Notes on the State of Virginia

shakespeare-brief-authority.text: but man, proud man, / Drest in a little brief authority, / Most ignorant of what he's most assured, / His glassy essence, like an angry ape, / Plays such fantastic tricks before high heaven / As make the angels weep
shakespeare-brief-authority.author: William Shakespeare

source.label: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (MIT)

dhammapada-elephant-in-battle.text: Silently shall I endure abuse as the elephant in battle endures the arrow sent from the bow: for the world is ill-natured

avot-strive-to-be-a-man.text: In a place where there are no men, strive to be a man

rights.note: Translation published at Sefaria under a CC BY licence.

washington-to-bigotry-no-sanction.text: It is now no more that toleration is spoken of, as if it was by the indulgence of one class of people, that another enjoyed the exercise of their inherent natural rights. For happily the Government of the United States, which gives to bigotry no sanction, to persecution no assistance, requires only that they who live under its protection should demean themselves as good citizens
washington-to-bigotry-no-sanction.author: George Washington
washington-to-bigotry-no-sanction.work: Letter to the Hebrew Congregation in Newport

rights.note: Letter of a President of the United States, 1790.

tacitus-mockery-of-every-sort.text: Mockery of every sort was added to their deaths. Covered with the skins of beasts, they were torn by dogs and perished, or were nailed to crosses, or were doomed to the flames and burnt, to serve as a nightly illumination, when daylight had expired
tacitus-mockery-of-every-sort.author: Tacitus
tacitus-mockery-of-every-sort.translator: Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb

mill-pleasant-falsehoods.text: the dictum that truth always triumphs over persecution, is one of those pleasant falsehoods which men repeat after one another till they pass into commonplaces, but which all experience refutes. History teems with instances of truth put down by persecution
mill-pleasant-falsehoods.author: John Stuart Mill

lowell-truth-on-the-scaffold.text: Truth forever on the scaffold, Wrong forever on the throne,— / Yet that scaffold sways the future, and, behind the dim unknown, / Standeth God within the shadow, keeping watch above his own
lowell-truth-on-the-scaffold.author: James Russell Lowell

burns-inhumanity-to-man.text: Many and sharp the num'rous ills / Inwoven with our frame! / More pointed still we make ourselves, / Regret, remorse, and shame! / And man, whose heaven-erected face / The smiles of love adorn, / Man's inhumanity to man / Makes countless thousands mourn
burns-inhumanity-to-man.author: Robert Burns

locke-care-of-souls.text: the care of souls does not belong to the magistrate. Not a magisterial care, I mean (if I may so call it), which consists in prescribing by laws and compelling by punishments
locke-care-of-souls.author: John Locke

universal-declaration-18.text: Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion; this right includes freedom to change his religion or belief, and freedom, either alone or in community with others and in public or private, to manifest his religion or belief in teaching, practice, worship and observance
universal-declaration-18.author: United Nations General Assembly

rights.note: Official public document of the United Nations.
